clue.text: Effect of legislation on one legislator

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it, so the legislation comes after

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws
an act is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: A question about how a new law affects a single lawmaker.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after; 'Effect' is the definition, not the legislation's result.
explanation.definitionFit: An impact is the influence or consequence something has, a synonym of effect.

clue.text: Lack of cultivation ruined grain once

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Once spoiled grain left the land uncultivated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cultivation' suggests farming, but it means education.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is a want of knowledge or refinement, the opposite of being cultured.

clue.text: Crucially important note to somebody held up

indicators.note: in a down clue, holding up raises the letters so the whole run reads from the bottom

parts.note: la is a note of the sol-fa scale
taken as written
a VIP, a very important person, is a somebody

explanation.surface: An important message sent to a celebrity has been delayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns the whole of LATOVIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pivotal acts as the hinge on which everything turns, so it is critical.

clue.text: Injury that's leading to knockout

parts.note: a cut is a minor wound
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A boxer's cut that leads to him being knocked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knockout' is boxing in the surface but means a stunner.
explanation.definitionFit: A knockout is a very attractive person, as is a cutie.

clue.text: What's put on board, is for the French to consume?

definitions.text: What's put on board, is for the French to consume?

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so the French word swallows the goods

parts.note: est is the French word for 'is'
cargo is the goods loaded aboard a ship

explanation.surface: A riddle about something served on the table for French diners.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes a snail dish served on a board (a menu or table) for French diners to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Escargot, the snail served as a delicacy in French restaurants, is food placed on a table for diners.

clue.text: In other words, foes stupidly entered outlaw territory

indicators.note: acting stupidly means behaving in a muddled way, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Enemies foolishly ventured into the bandits' country.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherwood Forest in Nottinghamshire is where the legendary outlaw Robin Hood lived with his band.

clue.text: Like Copperfield's friend, endlessly riding horse thus?

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: endlessly means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: Tommy Traddles is David's school friend in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A Dickensian question about how a character sits on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the final S from TRADDLES.
explanation.definitionFit: Astraddle means with a leg on each side, the posture of someone riding a horse.

clue.text: Undergo suffering for payment

indicators.note: the word under suffering is tormented into a new order

explanation.surface: Enduring pain in exchange for money.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerdon is an archaic word for a reward or recompense.

clue.text: Instructor's rebuke to junior soldiers

parts.note: tut is a sound of disapproval
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An officer's reprimand to recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher, an instructor.

clue.text: Head of Chambers at all bothered about being qualified to advocate?

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
about means moved around, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Whether a barristers' chambers' senior even cares about someone becoming a barrister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bothered' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'about' is the signal. In England a barrister is admitted by being called to the Bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Being admitted as a barrister qualifies a lawyer to plead cases in court.

clue.text: Probation making a small number corrupt

parts.note: No. is the short form of number, small meaning abbreviated
to vitiate is to spoil or corrupt

explanation.surface: A complaint that a trial period corrupts a few people.
explanation.definitionFit: A novitiate is the trial period served by a novice before taking vows, a period of probation.

clue.text: Amongst island races, we English are chirpy

indicators.note: being amongst the races places these letters inside them

parts.note: the TT races are held on the Isle of Man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheerful boast that the English are in good spirits among island races.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT (Tourist Trophy) is a famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds that tweet chirp, so the verb means to make chirping sounds.

clue.text: Ignoring the odds, urgent time to join up again

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters of the words leaves only the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: An instruction that it is high time to reunite.
explanation.definitionFit: To retie is to fasten or knot together once more.

clue.text: Rock 'n' roll awed a Sassenach, perhaps

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's reaction to rock music frightening the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' looks like part of the music; it is the anagram signal, and 'n' gives N. Highlanders called Lowland Scots Sassenachs, now a Scots word for the English.
explanation.definitionFit: To Gaelic-speaking Highlanders, a Sassenach was a Saxon, a name they also gave to the Scots of the southern plains.

clue.text: Redundant invalid

definitions.meaning: no longer having any use or force

explanation.definitionFit: The legal phrase means having no force, which covers both being superfluous and lacking validity.

clue.text: Job seeker keeping very quiet in Spanish port out East

indicators.note: keeping holds the other piece inside
out means the letter is left off

parts.note: Alicante is a port on Spain's east coast
pp, pianissimo, is the musical direction for very quiet

explanation.surface: Someone after work keeps a low profile in a Spanish harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' and 'keeping' both act here: the port loses its East, and what remains holds the very quiet music sign, leaving ALICANT around it.
explanation.definitionFit: An applicant is a person who applies for a job.

clue.text: Blunt, removing head of sword point

indicators.note: removing drops the named letter from the word

parts.note: snub means curt or blunt, as in a snub nose or a blunt rebuff

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A blunt sword with its tip broken off.
explanation.walkthrough: SNUB loses S, the first letter of 'sword'. 'point' looks like the sword's tip but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The nub of a matter is its central point or gist.

clue.text: Go to the country for an election

definitions.text: Go to the country for an election

parts.words: Go to the country for an election
parts.note: British politicians 'go to the country' when calling an election; here it is read as touring farmland to gather votes

explanation.definitionFit: To barnstorm is to tour rural districts making political speeches.

clue.text: I say! Look here!

indicators.note: say tells us to speak the word and take what it sounds like

parts.note: the pronoun as written

explanation.surface: Two exclamations calling for attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say!' is an old British exclamation, but here it means the pronoun said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye something is to look at it closely.

clue.text: Deeply involve little brother, cutting fruit-tree up

indicators.note: cutting into a word splits it open around the piece
in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom

parts.note: a lime is a citrus tree
bro is a short form of brother

explanation.surface: A boy chopping down a fruit tree gets into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives EMIL, which 'cutting' splits open around the little brother.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil is to entangle someone deeply in a conflict.

clue.text: One checking writings of academics with nothing to hide

indicators.note: a piece that hides another holds it inside

parts.note: a prof is a professor, a senior academic
O is zero, nothing
a reader is a British university rank just below professor

explanation.surface: Someone vetting scholars' papers who have no secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'academics' gives two ranks; 'to hide' puts O inside PROF. In British universities, a Reader is a senior lecturer below a professor.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader reads printed text to catch errors, so is a checker of written work.

clue.text: Childlike daughter's raised temperature far from normal

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word reads upwards

parts.note: naive means innocent like a child

explanation.surface: A girl's fever is abnormally high.
explanation.definitionFit: Deviant means departing from accepted standards, a long way off the norm.

clue.text: Press returned one… pound, grabbed by drug dealer

indicators.note: being grabbed by something places a piece inside it

parts.note: a pusher sells illegal drugs

indicators.note: returned means these letters run backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
lb is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: A news story of someone giving back a pound to a dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' gives BLI, which 'grabbed by' places inside the dealer; 'Press' means a publishing house, not newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A press, as in a university press, is a company that brings out books.

clue.text: Shelled out over a pound for cloth

indicators.note: over means covering, so one piece is placed around the other

parts.note: to shell out is to pay
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Paying more than a pound for fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaid is a tartan woollen cloth.

clue.text: Game in which score's four

parts.note: a score is twenty, which is four lots of five, and a handball game played in a walled court has that plural name

explanation.definitionFit: Fives is a British court game in which the ball is hit with the hand, and four fives make a score.

clue.text: Delicate fellow, superficial

parts.note: airy means light and lacking depth

explanation.surface: A frail man with a shallow nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy as an adjective means dainty and fragile, like a creature of folklore.

clue.text: Bouquet delivered from "Flora Romantica"

indicators.note: delivered from means letters are lifted out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Perfume sent from a romantic floral brand.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet is the pleasant smell of a wine, a synonym of a scent.

clue.text: Cruelly punish scholars, in trouble after a short time

indicators.note: after places the trouble following the time

parts.note: BAs are graduates, Bachelors of Arts
T is the abbreviation for time
taken as written
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Schoolboys facing a beating after being briefly in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To bastinado is to beat someone on the soles of the feet, a cruel punishment.

clue.text: What can stretch things out to a year? Time-wasting

parts.note: a dilator is an instrument that widens or stretches an opening
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A question about what could prolong something to a whole year.
explanation.definitionFit: Dilatory behaviour delays and causes delay, so it wastes time.

clue.text: Staunch follower of extremes in Stanislavsky "Method"

indicators.note: a follower comes after, so this piece is placed second
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: to stem a flow is to staunch it

explanation.surface: A loyal devotee of the Stanislavsky acting Method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch follower' looks like a loyal disciple, but staunch is a verb meaning to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is an organised method of doing things.
